### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

- **Target object** — the one open deployment job, in business words: "that job is still open on the
  practice's books"; "the deployment invoice". He offers identifiers on request: "He will read out
  the order the machines were bought on, NB-ORD dash five one zero eight eight three three, if that
  helps, and the serial on the rack label, PGD-FLEET-2211, if asked."
- **Timing** — this morning, explicitly: "he needs the deployment invoice settled this morning";
  "if asked whether the practice would rather leave it on the account to run to its terms he says
  no, he wants it cleared today."
- **Boundary of the action** — close off that job: "he wants it closed off".
- **Mode of authorisation** — a bank transfer, and expressly *not* the card: "the money will go out
  of the practice account as a transfer"; "if pressed for the card kept on file he says he thinks
  it ends 5744 but would rather the desk did not touch the card."
- **Simulator behaviour** — passive and conditional. "He responds rather than pushes." He supplies
  registered name and mobile unprompted and everything else on an if. He refuses to supply figures:
  "He cannot say what the crew's hours were on either day, nor what rate anyone was charged at, and
  he says plainly that the practice only sees the totals; he asks the desk to read those from its
  own record." He does not know the entitlement: "He has no idea how many included visits the
  contract has left and says as much." He confirms the refusal only if asked: "If the agent raises
  what the insurers said, he says the plan people wrote to them on Wednesday that they would not be
  covering it." He runs a handed-over tool at the agent's direction: "When the agent hands him
  something to run himself so that the transfer is recorded, he does it while they are talking and
  reads back the reference it gives him." He never names the rebill, the relief or their order.

### 4. Each scored parameter: formula in words, inputs, tiers, and value

#### 4.1 The labour rebilled after the refused claim — **1275.00 USD**, on 8.0 hours at 175.00

Baseline, `rebilled_labour_amount_computation_a582cd7b`: hours × rate, rounded to the cent, then
"the gross figure less what the plan has already paid out on the item", then "From the figure
rebilled come the write-offs that already stand on the job", then the diagnostic credit; "What
remains after those deductions, rounded to the nearest cent and never below nothing, is the labour
billed on the line."

Trigger: `labour_rebilled_as_chargeable_work_ece437f1` — "Where a plan's decision refuses a claim
after the work was carried out as plan work, the labour of that line is rebilled to the customer as
chargeable work." The decision `denied_not_covered` / `no_settlement` on `SC-CLM-77412` is a
refusal, and the 1051.25 write-off on ground `protection_plan_covered` shows the work was carried
out as plan work. It is no longer barred:
`one_billing_basis_per_line_of_work_4c2eb433` — "The clause that a customer cannot be billed for
labour on a line whose charge has been written off as plan covered is **no longer in force**,
having been superseded by the current basis for rebilling such a line."

- *Attendances of the refused line* — §1: "counted from the labour entries standing on the job
  other than those booked for the day the job was completed". `completed_date` is 2026-09-15, so
  the 437.50 entry drops out and the line carries labour for **two** attendance days, 2026-09-08
  and 2026-09-09.
- *Hours taken* — `hours_taken_for_a_rebilled_line_3bbf08ce`, first reading ("more than one
  attendance day"): "the hours recorded on the job are added and the hours recorded for the day it
  was completed are taken off them". (6.0 + 1.25 + 2.5) − 2.5 = **7.25 hours**.
- *How the minimum is applied* — `minimum_hours_on_a_rebilled_line_13d00493`, first reading
  ("more than one attendance day, a labour entry stands for the day the crew was dispatched, and
  the service requires two people to attend"). `crew_certification_and_site_readiness_8fb7c276`:
  Business On Site Deployment, "Two people must attend — yes". So "the service's minimum hours are
  applied to the day the crew was dispatched and to the hours of the line's later attendances taken
  together, and the two raised figures are added". `labour_tariff_and_chargeable_time_4ccb12d3`:
  "Least labour billed, hours" = 2.0 for this service. Dispatch day 6.0 → 6.0; the line's later
  attendance (2026-09-09) 1.25 → raised to 2.0; added = **8.0 hours**. (The partition is exactly
  the 7.25 hours taken: 6.0 + 1.25.)
- *Rate* — `rate_a_rebilled_line_carries_efd18b67`, first reading: "Where the labour of the day the
  crew was dispatched was recorded at any rate other than the service's own hourly rate, the
  service's own hourly rate is the rate." The 2026-09-08 entry records 145.00; the service's own
  rate is 175.00 (`labour_tariff_and_chargeable_time`). Rate = **175.00 USD an hour**. "The first
  line governs whatever the window and whatever surcharge stands on the job."
- *Gross* — 8.0 × 175.00 = **1400.00**.
- *What the gross is rebilled at* — `share_of_gross_rebilled_after_the_decision_6860ff52`, first
  reading: "Where the plan covering the item stands active and the decision recorded against its
  claim refused the claim, the whole of the gross figure is rebilled, to the extent of the
  per-claim limit the plan carries." `cover_limits_and_customer_excess_d44e35ec`: ShieldCare
  Business Fleet Protection, "Most on one claim, USD — 9000.00". 1400.00 is inside it →
  **1400.00**. The 620.00 payout is *not* deducted: it belongs to the third reading, which is
  reached only "Where neither situation holds", and it was paid on a different claim reference in
  any case.
- *Write-offs* — `writeoffs_standing_against_a_rebilled_figure_d10ee975`: "Where a write-off
  granted on the plan's cover stands on the job, nothing comes off." The 1051.25 is on that ground.
  **0.00**.
- *Diagnostic credit* — `diagnostic_fee_credit_against_a_rebill_eefaa864`: the 125.00 diagnostic
  fee is not more than the 1400.00 being rebilled, so the first reading fails; the second holds —
  "Where a diagnostic fee stands on the job and every diagnosis recorded on it found a fault, the
  diagnostic fees standing on the job are credited in full". Both `service_diagnostic_record`
  rows name a fault (`software_configuration`, `signal_or_network_fault`); neither is a diagnosis
  that "found no fault", the only thing the third line turns on. **125.00 credited**.
- 1400.00 − 0.00 − 125.00 = **1275.00 USD**.
  Tool `bill_uncovered_device_labour_51108cc0`: `visit_date` `2026-09-08` (§1 — "the entry the
  rebill books is stamped with the day the crew was dispatched, whatever attendances of that line
  its hours were drawn from"), `labour_hours` 8.0, `hourly_rate` 175.00, `labour_amount` 1275.00,
  `work_order_line_reference` `PGD-WO-5108833-L1` (the line the plan write-off and the dispatch-day

#### 4.2 The contract relief credited — **846.50 USD**

Baseline, `contract_relief_amount_computation_bf768af7`: a share of the chargeable labour billed on
the day the relief is granted, plus the attendance charges the contract does not leave with the
business, less what the plan has met, within the ceiling of the charges standing unsettled.

- *The pool* — `creditable_visits_from_the_contract_pool_79f2d5c4`: "the visits standing in that
  pool are the visits credited over the visit term of the service less the visits used over it".
  +2 credited, 1 used → **1 visit in the pool** (which matches the agreement's `visits_remaining`
  of 1).
- *Visits creditable* — the same document, first reading: "Where visits stand in that pool and
  visits granted under a plan covering the item stand among them, every visit standing in the pool
  is creditable." The grant's `visit_grant_reason` is `plan_included` and a plan covering
  `PGD-FLEET-2211` stands active. "The first reading takes precedence." **1 visit creditable.**
- *The share* — `share_of_rebilled_labour_the_visits_relieve_0f68aebc`: "The attendances rebilled
  are counted from the labour entries standing on the job other than those booked for the day it
  was completed and those booked on the day the relief is granted". The 437.50 entry is for the
  completion day and the new 1275.00 entry is booked *on* 2026-09-18, the day the relief is
  granted, so both drop out: **2 attendances rebilled** (2026-09-08, 2026-09-09). First reading
  ("visits stand creditable and the labour rebilled covers more than one attendance day"): "the
  visits creditable are set against the attendances rebilled and the share is the attendances they
  cover divided by the attendances rebilled" → 1 ÷ 2 = **0.5**.
- *Applied to* — §2: "That share is applied to the chargeable labour billed on the day the relief
  is granted" — the 1275.00 rebill booked today. 0.5 × 1275.00 = **637.50**.
- *Crew attendance charge added* — `crew_attendance_charge_added_to_contract_relief_584aa20f`,
  first reading: one `trip_charge` of 89.00 stands, and "the labour and parts booked for the day
  the crew was dispatched reach the figure at which the service waives it". Dispatch day 2026-09-08
  carries labour of 870.00 (and, once the rebill is booked, 1275.00 more) and no parts; the figure
  for Business On Site Deployment is 750.00 in both this document's own table and
  `crew_attendance_and_distance_charges_d17a1d70`. "The comparison of the first reading is a
  not-below-it one." → "that charge is added in full — every such charge standing on the job" =
  **89.00**.
- *Distance charge added* — `distance_charge_added_to_contract_relief_4e0cb275`, first reading:
  "Where such a charge stands on the job for the day the crew was dispatched, that charge is
  added." The `out_of_radius_fee` of 45.00 carries `visit_date` 2026-09-08. The record's own
  vocabulary ties it to the rule: `labour_billing_basis_and_settlement_d26ff6fe` clause 4 —
  "Mileage beyond the service's covered radius is billed at the service's rate for each mile beyond
  it" — and the annex's "Covered radius, miles". **45.00**.
- *Slot-move fee added* — `slot_move_fee_added_to_contract_relief_e281eb23`, first reading: a
  `reschedule_fee` of 75.00 stands and no write-off on the retailer's own error stands against it
  (the only write-off is `protection_plan_covered`), so "that fee is added in full" = **75.00**.
  (`appointment_booking_figures_0251ca2a` gives this service's slot-move fee as 75.00, matching.)
- *What the plan has met* — `what_the_plan_has_met_of_the_same_work_39cb3eb3`, first reading:
  "Where the plan covering the item stands active and the decision recorded against its claim
  refused the claim, nothing is taken off, because a refused claim has met nothing of the work" —
  and expressly "Nothing is taken off, even where a write-off on the plan's cover stands on the
  job." **0.00**.
- 637.50 + 89.00 + 45.00 + 75.00 − 0.00 = **846.50**.
- *The ceiling* — §5: charges standing unsettled = (2167.75 + 1275.00) − 400.00 − 1051.25 =
  1991.50, which the tool confirms as the job's outstanding figure after the rebill. 846.50 is
  below it. Relief = **846.50 USD**.
  Tool `credit_contract_relief_ce7af535`, `relief_ground` `contract_term`
  ("a term of the customer's business contract requires the charge to be relieved"),
  `work_order_line_reference` `PGD-WO-5108833-L1`.

against those charges, less what is left for its next invoice and less what the plan has met of the

- *What is left for the next invoice* — `charges_left_for_the_next_business_invoice_fcc032e6`,

- *What the plan has met* — `what_the_plan_has_met_on_a_business_invoice_bfa6608a`, first reading:

- (2763.75 + 345.00 + 334.00) − 1897.75 − 400.00 − 0.00 − 0.00 = **1145.00 USD**, above nothing.
  Tool `settle_deployment_invoice_642fded5` (user-owned), `payment_amount` 1145.00,

**Terminal state, verified by executing the sequence against a throwaway engine for this task:**
the returns read "Outstanding service charges on the job are now 1991.50 USD", "… now 1145.00 USD",
"… now 0.00 USD". The job clears to nothing.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

```
settle the invoice standing on the job   (the customer's own request, his own write)
  └── waits on: the relief the business contract owes standing recorded against the job's charges
        └── waits on: the chargeable labour the plan's refusal sends back, standing billed on the
                      job on the day the relief is granted
```

Handling order: rebill the refused labour → credit the contract relief → record the transfer.

**Hop A — the settlement waits on the contract relief. Marked: state-derived.**
- The prerequisite sentence, in the hub of the problem it blocks
  (`settling_the_invoice_standing_on_a_job_7f77327a`): "The figure the invoice settles is worked out
  only after the relief the business contract owes stands recorded against the job's charges."
  Same-form restatement in the same document: "Until that relief stands recorded against the job's
  charges, the figure the invoice settles is not worked out."
- A **state**: a relief owed by the contract standing recorded. No action, no tool, no policy named.
- Does it hold? `find_service_events` shows one `service_waiver`, ground `protection_plan_covered`.
  Nothing on a contract term stands. Unmet.
- Which write brings it about? The words "relief", "business contract" reach
  `relief_credited_under_a_business_contract_11031f7a`: "A business profile holding a … job may be
  relieved of part of what that job has billed it, where its contract carries included visits and
  where the attendance charges the job has raised are charges the contract does not leave with the
  business", and "The relief stands on the job as a write-off entry naming the ground it rests on".
  The ground vocabulary matches the record's `waiver_reason` field: `contract_term` — "a term of the
  customer's business contract requires the charge to be relieved". And the condition holds on the
  records: the agreement carries `visits_remaining` 1, and the job carries a `trip_charge`, an
  `out_of_radius_fee` and a `reschedule_fee`.

**Hop B — the contract relief waits on the rebilled labour. Marked: state-derived.**
- The prerequisite sentence, in the hub of the problem it blocks
  (`relief_credited_under_a_business_contract_11031f7a`): "The relief is fixed only once the
  chargeable labour the plan's refusal sends back to the customer stands billed on the job on the
  day the relief is granted." Same-form restatement in the same document: "Until such a labour
  charge stands billed on the job on that day, the relief is not fixed."
- A **state**: a chargeable labour charge, arising from the plan's refusal, standing billed on the
  job, dated today. It names no tool and no policy.
- Does it hold? Every labour entry on the job is dated 2026-09-08, -09 or -15; none is booked on
  2026-09-18. Unmet.
- Which write brings it about? The words "chargeable", "labour", "the plan's refusal" reach
  `labour_rebilled_as_chargeable_work_ece437f1`: "Where a plan's decision refuses a claim after the
  work was carried out as plan work, the labour of that line is rebilled to the customer as
  chargeable work. The rebill stands on the job as a labour entry of its own … and raises the
  service charges outstanding on the job by the amount billed." And the refusal is on the records:
  `claim_decision` `denied_not_covered` against `SC-CLM-77412`, the reference the agreement itself
  carries in `protection_plan_reference`. The persona corroborates it when asked: "the plan people
  wrote to them on Wednesday that they would not be covering it, and that this is exactly why he is
  ringing."
- The chain is also what makes the relief non-trivial: §2 of the relief's computation applies the
  share to "the chargeable labour billed on the day the relief is granted", which is nothing until
  hop B is done.

**No hop is action-named, and no hop is pre-solved.** Each of the six discoverable tool names
occurs in exactly one document, its own hub. No document lists the three writes, states the order,
or points from one problem to another.

### Verdict

**KB-RUNTIME PASS.** All three scored figures, the hours and the rate carried on the rebill entry,
every line reference and attendance day, both write-off grounds, the payment method and the owner
of each call agree exactly with the source layer, as do the tree, the handling order and the
terminal state. Nothing required hidden compute, GT or the raw `initial_state`; no second equally
reasonable reading was found; both declared prerequisites are carried at the same strength; every
declared factor is entailed and reachable from the words the records use.

Three readings that were tight during the derivation, all of which the corpus does close, are
recorded as observations and carried into `policy_kb/1.md`:

1. **The line's "later attendances" and the completion day.** `minimum_hours_on_a_rebilled_line`
   speaks of "the hours of the line's later attendances taken together" without restating that the
   line's attendances exclude the completion day. That exclusion is stated in the computation
   document's own §1 ("The attendances of the refused line are counted from the labour entries
   standing on the job other than those booked for the day the job was completed") and in
   `hours_taken_for_a_rebilled_line`, and the factor's own illustration confirms that two
   attendance days give exactly one later attendance. Had the completion day's 2.5 hours been drawn
   in, the hours would have been 9.75 and the rebill 1581.25 rather than 1275.00.
2. **"Every diagnosis found a fault."** The corpus never publishes the diagnostic-code vocabulary,
   so a reader judges from the codes recorded. The source's test is the single negative
   `diagnostic_code='no_fault_found'`, and the corpus carries it as a negative test rather than a
   positive one — `diagnostic_fee_credit_against_a_rebill`'s point of judgement reads "No diagnosis
   recorded on the job found no fault, so the second reading holds". That is what makes the reading
   single for the two codes on this job.
3. **"The service's minimum hours" versus "Least labour billed, hours."** The figure that raises
   1.25 hours to 2.0 — and so moves the rebill from 7.25 hours to 8.0 — is the source parameter
   `minimum_labour_hours`, published in `labour_tariff_and_chargeable_time_4ccb12d3` under the
   column heading "Least labour billed, hours". The bridge to "the service's minimum hours" is
   `labour_billing_basis_and_settlement_d26ff6fe`'s closing paragraph, which names "the minimum
   hours" among the per-service figures carried in the labour schedule. It is the corpus's weakest
   naming link on this task.
